# IC Reactor Full LLM Guide

Use this file when an AI assistant needs enough context to write or review IC
Reactor code without reading the whole repository. Use `llms.txt` first for a
compact manifest and package routing table.

## What IC Reactor Is

IC Reactor v3 is a TypeScript/React monorepo for Internet Computer apps. It wraps
typed canister calls with TanStack Query caching, reusable query/mutation
objects, React hooks, optional Internet Identity auth helpers, runtime Candid
parsing, and code generation from `.did` files.

This documentation targets the stable `@ic-reactor/core` v3.12.5 runtime release.

## Package Boundaries

| Package                   | Responsibility                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@ic-reactor/core`        | Framework-agnostic runtime with `ClientManager`, `Reactor`, `DisplayReactor`, and `@tanstack/query-core` integration. No React imports. |
| `@ic-reactor/react`       | React hooks, `createActorHooks`, query/mutation factories, Internet Identity auth, and identity-attribute hooks.                         |
| `@ic-reactor/candid`      | Runtime Candid fetching/parsing adapters, `CandidReactor`, display variants, and metadata reactors.                                     |
| `@ic-reactor/parser`      | Rust/WASM Candid parser. One entrypoint (`@ic-reactor/parser`); conditional exports pick the browser or Node build.                     |
| `@ic-reactor/codegen`     | Shared generator pipeline for declarations, reactor files, stable wrappers, and client helpers.                                         |
| `@ic-reactor/cli`         | CLI around `@ic-reactor/codegen`, config loading, commands, and schema.                                                                 |
| `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` | Vite watch-mode generation and local IC environment injection.                                                                          |

## Install

React apps:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/react-query
```

`@ic-reactor/react` needs `@tanstack/react-query` 5.90.2 or later and React 18
or later. IC Reactor needs TypeScript 5.7 or later: its declarations, and those
of `@icp-sdk/core`, use generic typed arrays such as `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>`,
which TypeScript 5.7 introduced.

Non-React apps:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/core @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/query-core
```

Auth helpers:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/auth@^10
```

The `@icp-sdk/auth` peer is `^8.0.0 || ^10.0.0`. Install v10: it is the first
release to peer `@icp-sdk/core@^6`, so a strict `npm install` resolves the set
with no `overrides`. v7 and v9 are not supported — v9 still peers
`@icp-sdk/core@^5`.

On v8, a strict `npm install` fails with `ERESOLVE` (stale metadata rather than
an actual incompatibility — auth v8 runs against core v6). For npm on v8, add to
`package.json`:

```json
{ "overrides": { "@icp-sdk/auth": { "@icp-sdk/core": "$@icp-sdk/core" } } }
```

IC Reactor keeps one options contract across both majors and translates at the
boundary. On v10 four constructor options are dropped with a warning because
they have no equivalent: `storage`, `keyType`, `idleOptions`, `identity`. And
`targets` on `login()` is ignored by v10 — the delegation is NOT restricted to
those canisters. Pin `^8` if you depend on canister-scoped delegations.
`maxTimeToIdle` on `login()` and `disableBrowserActivity` on the client exist
only on v10, so IC Reactor forwards them to v10 and drops them on v8 with a
warning. On v10 a custom `identityProvider` also needs `internetIdentityId`,
because v10 names a provider by its authorize URL and its canister. Off
mainnet, IC Reactor points v10's own minting agent at the app's replica and has
it fetch that network's root key, or gives it the app's own
`agentOptions.rootKey` when the `ClientManager` was given one. The real-client suite runs the actual
`AuthClient` under both majors, against a fake Internet Identity and a fake
replica that certifies v10's mint and revoke calls. A deployed Internet
Identity canister is not part of it.

Dynamic Candid:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/candid @ic-reactor/parser
```

## One-Call Setup

`defineReactor` creates the `QueryClient`, `ClientManager`, reactor, and bound
hooks in one call. `defineDisplayReactor` takes the same options and builds a
`DisplayReactor` instead of a `Reactor`. `defineReactor({ display: true })` is
deprecated; never generate it. Plain `defineReactor` is not deprecated, although
typescript-eslint's `no-deprecated` also reports references such as
`typeof defineReactor`: do not switch a raw-value setup to
`defineDisplayReactor` to silence it, since that turns bigints and principals
into strings.

```ts
import { defineDisplayReactor } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { canisterId, idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const backendApp = defineDisplayReactor<_SERVICE>({
  name: "backend",
  idlFactory,
  // Required unless the Vite plugin injects an `ic_env` cookie for this
  // canister on a local replica. Without it the reactor constructor throws
  // `canisterId is required for "backend"` on a server and on any deployed
  // origin.
  canisterId,
})

export const {
  reactor: backend,
  queryClient,
  useActorQuery,
  useActorMutation,
  useActorMethod,
  useAuth,
  useIdentityAttributes,
} = backendApp
```

It returns the six `createActorHooks` hooks plus `useAuth`, `useAgentState`,
`useUserPrincipal`, `useIdentityAttributes`, and the underlying `reactor`,
`clientManager`, `queryClient`, `authentication`, and `identityAttributes`.
`authentication` and `identityAttributes` are lazy getters, so the optional
`@icp-sdk/auth` peer is only loaded once auth is actually touched. Omitting the
peer builds everywhere; webpack-family bundlers print one `Module not found`
warning for it because the import is declared optional, silenceable with
`ignoreWarnings: [{ module: /@ic-reactor\/react/, message: /@icp-sdk\/auth/ }]`.

To share one agent and one Internet Identity session across canisters, pass the
first result's `authentication` into the next call:

```ts
import {
  canisterId as indexCanisterId,
  idlFactory as indexIdl,
  type _SERVICE as _INDEX,
} from "./declarations/index_canister"

export const indexApp = defineReactor<_INDEX>({
  name: "index",
  idlFactory: indexIdl,
  canisterId: indexCanisterId,
  authentication: backendApp.authentication,
})
```

Passing `authentication` alone is enough — its `clientManager` is adopted.
Passing a *different* `clientManager` alongside it throws, because sign-in would
update one agent while the reactor calls through another.

## Manual Runtime Setup

Use this when construction order or dependency injection needs to be explicit.

```ts
// A React app imports the runtime through @ic-reactor/react, which re-exports
// @ic-reactor/core; with the React install above, @ic-reactor/core and
// @tanstack/query-core are not direct dependencies and do not resolve under pnpm.
import {
  ClientManager,
  DisplayReactor,
  createActorHooks,
} from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { canisterId, idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const queryClient = new QueryClient()
export const clientManager = new ClientManager({ queryClient })

export const backend = new DisplayReactor<_SERVICE>({
  clientManager,
  idlFactory,
  name: "backend",
  canisterId, // required outside the Vite plugin's local `ic_env` cookie
})

export const { useActorQuery, useActorMutation } = createActorHooks(backend)
```

Use `DisplayReactor` for UI/form code. Use `Reactor` when raw Candid values are
required.

For other canisters of the same interface (several ICRC ledgers),
`reactor.forCanister(canisterId)` returns a memoized sibling of the same class
on the same `ClientManager`, whose calls and query keys use its own canister;
the same id always gives the same object, so it is safe in render and `useMemo`
deps. Use it instead of retargeting a shared reactor with `setCanisterId`, and
do not add the canister id to `queryKey` (keys already start with it).

Derive types from a reactor instead of copying shapes by hand:
`ReactorArgsOf<typeof backend, "get_profile">` (args in the reactor's own form),
`ReactorDataOf<...>` (what `callMethod`, a mutation and `execute()` resolve
with) and `ReactorErrorOf<...>` (a hook's `error` type), plus `ServiceOf` and
`TransformOf`. They read reactor instances, not query or mutation objects.

## Pattern Selection

| Need                              | Preferred API                                  | Works outside React                                                |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Component hooks with one canister | `defineReactor(params)`, `defineDisplayReactor(params)` | No                                                        |
| Server-rendered app               | `createReactorProvider(factory)`               | No                                                                 |
| Explicit construction order       | `ClientManager` + `Reactor` + `createActorHooks` | No                                                               |
| Generic component hooks           | `createActorHooks(reactor)`                    | No                                                                 |
| Method-specific reusable reads (query methods) | `createQuery`, `createSuspenseQuery`, `createQueryFactory` | Yes: `.fetch()`, `.prefetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()` |
| Paginated reads                   | `createInfiniteQuery`, suspense variant        | Yes: `.fetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()`                |
| Reusable updates                  | `createMutation`                               | Yes: `.execute(args)`                                              |
| One imperative component call API | `useActorMethod`                               | No                                                                 |
| Larger `.did`-driven apps         | `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` or `@ic-reactor/cli` | Generated hooks: no. With `factories: true`, the generated query/mutation objects: yes (`.fetch()`, `.execute()`) |

A "read" is a query method, or an update method that is safe to repeat such as
a certified read. State-changing update methods go through `createMutation`,
`useActorMutation` or `useActorMethod`: a query runs its method again on every
refetch (mount, window focus, reconnect, invalidation), and every run of an
update executes on the canister.

When a query's args are not known yet, pass TanStack Query's `skipToken`
(re-exported by `@ic-reactor/react`) in their place; the query makes no call
until they arrive:

```tsx
import { skipToken } from "@ic-reactor/react"

const { data } = useActorQuery({
  functionName: "get_user",
  args: userId ? [userId] : skipToken,
})
```

Infinite hooks take `getArgs: owner ? (start) => [...] : skipToken`, and
`createQueryFactory` takes `getBalance(owner ? [account] : skipToken)`, which
for `skipToken` returns an object with only `useQuery()`. The suspense hooks,
`createQuery` and `createSuspenseQuery` do not take it. Never call `refetch()`
on a skipped query.

## Inside React vs Outside React

Only call React hooks inside React components or custom hooks:

- `useActorQuery`
- `useActorMutation`
- `useActorMethod`
- `.useQuery()`
- `.useMutation()`
- `.useSuspenseQuery()`
- `.useInfiniteQuery()`

Outside React, use imperative methods:

- query `.fetch()`, `.prefetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()`,
  `.setData()` (`.prefetch()` and `.setData()` are not on infinite query
  objects), and `.cancel()`, `.reset()`, `.optimisticUpdate()` on its own entry
- mutation `.execute(args)`
- reactor `.fetchQuery()`, `.getQueryData()`, `.invalidateQueries()`,
  `.callMethod()`

`query.fetch()` and `reactor.fetchQuery()` fetch again, at most 3 times, when
a sign-in or sign-out switches the principal mid-fetch (after that they reject
with a `CallError`). Wrap a hand-written fetch that goes straight to the
`QueryClient` (`queryClient.fetchQuery`, `fetchInfiniteQuery`,
`ensureQueryData`) in `clientManager.fetchAcrossIdentitySwitch(() => ...)`:
unwrapped, a switch can resolve it with the previous principal's cached data.
`useActorMethod`'s `call()` is not protected this way; loaders and services use
`query.fetch()` or `reactor.fetchQuery()`.

In tests, render hooks with `renderHook` / `render` or call the imperative APIs
on a real reactor backed by the fake replica from `@ic-reactor/core/testing`
(`@ic-reactor/react/testing` in a React app). Install it before any
`ClientManager` or agent is built, and do not stub a `Reactor`:

```ts
import { createTestCanister, installFakeReplica } from "@ic-reactor/core/testing"

const replica = installFakeReplica({
  canisters: {
    [canisterId]: createTestCanister<_SERVICE>(idlFactory, {
      greet: ([name]) => `Hello, ${name}!`,
    }),
  },
})
// ...then build the ClientManager and reactor; call replica.restore() in afterEach
```

Handlers get the decoded args and `{ caller }` and return the raw Candid
result: `{ Err }` reaches the reactor as a `CanisterError`, a throw as a
`CallError`.

## Reusable Factory Example

```ts
import { createMutation, createQueryFactory } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { backend } from "./reactor"

export const getProfile = createQueryFactory(backend, {
  functionName: "get_profile",
})

export const updateProfile = createMutation(backend, {
  functionName: "update_profile",
})
```

Inside React:

```tsx
const profileQuery = getProfile(["alice"])
const { data } = profileQuery.useQuery()
const { mutateAsync } = updateProfile.useMutation({
  // The factory covers every cached profile, whatever its args
  invalidateQueries: [getProfile],
})
```

Outside React:

```ts
const profileQuery = getProfile(["alice"])
await profileQuery.fetch()
const cached = profileQuery.getCacheData()
await updateProfile.execute([{ name: "Alice" }])
await profileQuery.invalidate()
```

A mutation's `invalidateQueries` (`createMutation` config, `.useMutation()`
options, `useActorMutation`, `useActorMethod`) takes a query object
(`[profileQuery]`), a query factory (`[getProfile]`, every args instance), or a
descriptor `{ functionName, args? }` of the mutation's own reactor, keyed at the
canister the mutation was sent to. It is awaited before `onSuccess`. Never
hand-write a key such as `["get_profile"]`: every key starts with the canister
id, so it matches nothing. A query factory also has `getQueryKey()` (the prefix
of all its instances) and `invalidate()`.

`query.invalidate()`, a factory's `invalidate()` and
`reactor.invalidateQueries(...)` return a `Promise` that resolves once the
active matches have refetched (a failed refetch does not reject it). Prefix a
fire-and-forget call with `void`.

For optimistic UI, return `getPost([postId]).optimisticUpdate((post) => ...)`
from `onMutate`, call `rollback()` on it in `onError`, and invalidate the query
in `onSettled`. Do not hand-roll `cancelQueries` / `setQueryData` snapshots,
and use `reactor.queryClient` rather than `useQueryClient()`.

`createQuery`, `createSuspenseQuery` and the query factories take `callConfig`
(`canisterId`, `agent`, `effectiveCanisterId`) as the hooks do, for the call and
the key: `createQuery(ledger, { functionName: "icrc1_symbol", callConfig: { canisterId: ckbtcId } })`.
In a codegen project, `factories: true` generates these objects (see Code
Generation).

## Auth

`@ic-reactor/react` owns `AuthenticationManager`,
`IdentityAttributesManager`, auth constants/types, and React hooks over those
managers.

```ts
import {
  AuthenticationManager,
  IdentityAttributesManager,
  createAuthHooks,
  createIdentityAttributeHooks,
} from "@ic-reactor/react"

export const authentication = new AuthenticationManager({ clientManager })
export const { useAuth, useAgentState, useUserPrincipal } =
  createAuthHooks(authentication)

export const identityAttributes = new IdentityAttributesManager(authentication)
export const { useIdentityAttributes } =
  createIdentityAttributeHooks(identityAttributes)
```

`createAuthHooks` takes an `AuthenticationManager`, never a `ClientManager`, and
returns exactly `useAuth`, `useAgentState`, and `useUserPrincipal`.
`useIdentityAttributes` comes only from `createIdentityAttributeHooks`.

`useAuth()` reports `isAuthenticating: true` from the first render, and in
every server render, until the manager's first session restore settles (a
failed restore counts as settled). Guard a protected route
with `if (isAuthenticating)` before `if (!isAuthenticated)`; there is no
separate ready flag. `authentication.authState` read outside React starts at
`isAuthenticating: false`.

`authentication.dispose()` releases the Internet Identity client the manager
built (never a caller's `authClient`). It does not sign out, and a later
`login()`, `logout()` or `prepareClient()` builds a new client, so it is safe
in a StrictMode effect cleanup. `createReactorProvider` calls it for the
managers built for its value when the tree unmounts.

Pass identity-attribute nonces as a callback. Awaiting the nonce before the call
ends the user gesture and the browser blocks the Internet Identity window. The
callback must resolve to the nonce's bytes. A `DisplayReactor` (what
`defineDisplayReactor` builds, and what `backend` is above) returns a `blob` as a hex
string, so convert it with `hexToUint8Array`. A raw `Reactor` already returns a
`Uint8Array`, and there `nonce: () => backend.callMethod({ ... })` is enough.

```ts
import { hexToUint8Array } from "@ic-reactor/react"

await identityAttributes.request({
  keys: ["email"],
  nonce: async () =>
    hexToUint8Array(
      await backend.callMethod({ functionName: "register_begin" })
    ),
})
```

### Local Internet Identity

`localInternetIdentityProvider(port, canisterId?, authorizePath?)` builds
`http://<canisterId>.localhost:<port>/authorize`. Which path works depends on the
installed II build, so `AuthenticationManager.prepareClient()` probes the
canister over the agent and selects `/authorize` or the legacy `/#authorize`, and
rejects login outright when the build serves neither.

Only builds up to `release-2026-03-16` work locally: `release-2025-03-07` and
earlier serve the SPA at `/` with a `#authorize` fragment, `release-2026-01-05`
through `release-2026-03-16` serve `/authorize`, and from `release-2026-03-23` the
frontend left the canister entirely (the id.ai split). A local login that hangs on
the gateway's "Response Verification Error" page is an unsupported II build —
install `internet_identity_dev.wasm` from `release-2026-03-16`.

## Error Handling (Important)

IC Reactor distinguishes canister business errors from transport/runtime errors.

| Error kind | Typical source | Preferred handling |
| ---------- | -------------- | ------------------ |
| `CanisterError` | `Result.Err` returned by canister methods | `onCanisterError` (for hooks/factories), or `isCanisterError(...)` in try/catch |
| `CallError` | network/agent issues (timeouts, unreachable canister, etc.) | `onError` or `isCallError(...)` |
| `ValidationError` | `DisplayReactor` argument validators | `isValidationError(...)` and show field errors |

`CanisterError` carries the raw canister error value on `.err` — not `.detail`,
`.data`, or `.message`. `.code` is the variant key, or the `code` field when the
payload follows the ApiError shape. `.details` is that payload's own `details`
field as decoded (never a `Map`: `[] | [Array<[string, string]>]` for an
`opt vec record { text; text }` from a `Reactor`, a plain object from a
`DisplayReactor`), and `undefined` for a payload without a text `code`. Always
read the payload from `.err`.

When using mutations, prefer:

- `onCanisterError` for logic errors from canister `Err` variants
- `onError` for broad fallback handling across all error types

Do not use only `onError` when business logic needs distinct UX messaging.

Retries: `reactorRetry` (predicate `isRetryableReactorError`) is the query
default of the `QueryClient` that `defineReactor` and `defineDisplayReactor`
create. In a browser it retries transport, certificate, HTTP 5xx/408/429 and
SysTransient/SysUnknown failures up to 3 times, and never a `CanisterError`, a
`ValidationError`, an encode/decode failure, or any other HTTP 4xx (an expired
delegation's 400, a 403). An update method run through a query with no `retry`
of its own retries only a SysTransient rejection, within the `QueryClient`'s
retry default (`reactor.getQueryRetry(functionName, queryKey)`). Mutations retry
nothing unless `retry` is set, and a `QueryClient` `mutations.retry` default
applies unchanged to `useActorMutation`, `createMutation` (hook and
`execute()`) and `useActorMethod` update calls. Each retry of an update is a
new call the canister runs, so use `retry: reactorUpdateRetry` (predicate
`isRetryableUpdateError`), which retries only SysTransient.

## Code Generation

Use generated hooks when canisters are large, `.did` files change often, or
consistent typed exports matter.

| Tool                      | Use when                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` | Vite app, watch-mode regeneration, local environment injection                |
| `@ic-reactor/cli`         | Non-Vite app, CI, explicit generation command                                 |
| `@ic-reactor/codegen`     | Internal/shared generator pipeline; app users usually do not call it directly |

Generated canister directories usually contain declaration files, a managed
`index.generated.ts`, and a stable `index.ts` wrapper. Put custom app logic in
wrapper modules or factory files, not generated files.

Set `factories: true` on a canister (`canisters.<key>.factories` in
`ic-reactor.json`, or a Vite plugin `canisters[]` entry; needs
`target: "react"`) to also write a managed `index.factories.generated.ts` with
one object per method, bound to the generated reactor: `<camelMethod>Query`
(`createQuery` for a query method without args, `createQueryFactory` with args)
and `<camelMethod>Mutation` (`createMutation`) for update and oneway methods.
The default `index.ts` re-exports it; to change one factory, export the same
name from `index.ts`. Prefer it over hand-written per-method factory modules.
Each call is `/* @__PURE__ */`, so unused factories are dropped from the
bundle. Like `index.generated.ts`, the objects are module scope, so they are
client-only.

### Codegen Consumer Flow

1. Configure `ic-reactor.json` (CLI) or `icReactor(...)` (Vite plugin).
2. Generate canister files.
3. Treat `index.generated.ts` as managed output.
4. Keep app-specific logic in `index.ts` or adjacent factory modules.
5. Re-run generation after `.did` changes.

Use CLI for explicit CI/manual generation; use Vite plugin for watch-mode local
development.

## Dynamic Candid

Use `@ic-reactor/candid` for explorers, dev tools, unknown canisters, metadata
forms, or Candid strings discovered at runtime. Use `@ic-reactor/parser` when
local `.did` parsing is needed; it ships WASM builds for browser and Node.js.

### Parser Import Path

`@ic-reactor/parser` has a single entrypoint:

```ts
import { didToJs, parseDid, validateIDL } from "@ic-reactor/parser"
```

There are no `/web`, `/nodejs`, or `/bundler` subpath exports — the package's
`exports` map declares only `"."` and `"./package.json"`. Conditional exports
pick the build: `browser`/`workerd`/default resolve to `dist/web`, and `node`
resolves to `dist/nodejs`. Do not deep-import `dist/`.

### Common Candid Patterns

Agents should account for these patterns in generated TypeScript:

- `Result` variants (`Ok`/`Err`, `ok`/`err`) are already unwrapped by the Reactor: `data` is the
  Ok payload, and an `Err` throws a `CanisterError` instead of ever reaching `data`. Do not write
  `"Ok" in data` guards — they can never be true. `callMethod()` unwraps too, so it is not an
  escape hatch; overriding `transformResult` on a Reactor subclass is the only way to receive the
  raw variant
- numeric Candid values (`nat`, `int`, etc.) are usually `bigint` in raw mode and strings in display mode.
  Ledger amounts are base units (e8s): show them with `formatTokenAmount(value, decimals)` (exact; `maxFractionDigits`
  truncates) and read typed text with `parseTokenAmount(text, decimals)`, which returns a `bigint` (send
  `.toString()` to a `DisplayReactor`) and throws on bad text. Both come from `@ic-reactor/core`, re-exported by
  `@ic-reactor/react`
- `principal` values are `Principal` in raw mode and strings in display mode. Validate typed principal text with
  `isPrincipalText(text.trim())`, not a `try` around `Principal.fromText`
- `opt T` often appears as tuples/options in raw actor shapes; UI flows should normalize these carefully
- large nested variants/records are common in ledger/governance canisters and benefit from reusable query/mutation factories

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- Calling React hooks in loaders/actions/services (hook tests render them with `renderHook`)
- Hard-coding query keys such as `["get_posts"]` (keys start with the canister id): pass query objects, query
  factories or `{ functionName, args? }` to `invalidateQueries`
- Passing a state-changing update method to a query hook or query factory (`useActorQuery`, `createQuery`,
  `createQueryFactory`, the infinite and suspense variants): it re-executes on every refetch; use a mutation
- A numeric `retry` on an update mutation, on `useActorMethod`, or as a `QueryClient` `mutations.retry` default:
  each retry is a new call the canister runs; use `retry: reactorUpdateRetry`
- `args: [userId!]`, placeholder args, or `as any` plus `enabled` for args not known yet: pass `skipToken`
- `Number(x) / 10 ** decimals`, `parseFloat`, `Math.pow` or `toFixed` token math: use `formatTokenAmount` /
  `parseTokenAmount`
- Retargeting a shared reactor with `setCanisterId` for several tokens: use `reactor.forCanister(canisterId)`
- Generating `defineReactor({ display: true })`: use `defineDisplayReactor`
- Stubbing a `Reactor` (`as unknown as Reactor`) in tests: use `@ic-reactor/core/testing`
- Editing `index.generated.ts` or `index.factories.generated.ts` files directly
- Choosing raw `Reactor` for UI/form flows when display values were intended
- Duplicating codegen logic in app code instead of using CLI/Vite plugin configuration

## Example Routing by App Framework

| App stack | Recommended path |
| --------- | ---------------- |
| Vite + React | `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` + generated declarations/hooks |
| Next.js (pages/app router) | CLI generation + factories; hooks in `"use client"` modules. On the server build the reactor per request with `createReactorProvider` (see SSR rule below) |
| TanStack Router | query/mutation factories with `.fetch()` for loaders and `.useQuery()` for components |
| Plain TS/node scripts | `@ic-reactor/core` + imperative APIs (`callMethod`, `fetchQuery`, `invalidateQueries`) |

### SSR rule

A reactor owns its `QueryClient`, and query keys are
`[canisterId, functionName, args]` (plus a `{ transform }` segment on a
`DisplayReactor`, and an `{ agent: n }` segment when `callConfig.agent` is not
the `ClientManager`'s own agent) with no caller principal. A module-scope
reactor on a server is therefore shared by every request, so a cached
caller-scoped result (`get_my_balance`, deposit address, `my_profile`) is served
to the next request. `AuthenticationManager` is built from a `ClientManager` and
signs in on that manager's agent, so it belongs in the same request as its
`ClientManager`. On the server it loads no auth client and stays signed out
unless app code signs in there, and a module-scope one would then leave that
identity on the agent every request signs with. (The auth hooks themselves
render a fixed state on the server: signed out, with `isAuthenticating: true`,
the state a browser shows until its session restore settles.)

Under SSR/RSC, construct the reactor, `ClientManager`, and
`AuthenticationManager` inside the request. A bare call in a module body is still
module scope, so use `createReactorProvider(factory)`. It runs the factory in a
`useState` initializer, once per mounted provider (a server render is its own
tree, so once per request), disposes the `AuthenticationManager`s built for its
value when the tree unmounts, and renders a `QueryClientProvider` for the
value's `QueryClient`. `examples/nextjs/src/service/provider.tsx` does this:

```tsx
"use client"
import { createReactorProvider, defineReactor } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { canisterId, idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const { ReactorProvider, useReactor } = createReactorProvider(() =>
  defineReactor<_SERVICE>({ name: "backend", idlFactory, canisterId })
)

// app/layout.tsx (a server component): <ReactorProvider>{children}</ReactorProvider>

export function Profile() {
  const { useActorQuery } = useReactor()
  const { data } = useActorQuery({ functionName: "get_my_profile" })
  return <h1>{data?.name}</h1>
}
```

`ReactorProvider` and `useReactor` are what the app destructures from
`createReactorProvider`, not package exports. The factory may return a record
(`{ backend, ledger, profile }`, with query objects built inside it), read with
`useReactor("ledger")`. It receives the provider's props other than `children`,
read once per mount; give the provider a new `key` to build again. Call
`createReactorProvider` at module scope, never inside a component. A provider
mounted by a transition needs its own `<Suspense>` boundary inside it around
suspending components.

Module scope stays correct for client-only SPAs. Hooks are client-only; they
also bind to their reactor's own `QueryClient`, so `HydrationBoundary` prefetch
does not reach them unless the provider's client is that same instance. Below
`createReactorProvider`'s provider it is; pass
`createReactorProvider(factory, { queryClientProvider: false })` to keep an
outer `QueryClientProvider` instead.

A React Server Component, server action or route handler may import `Reactor`,
`DisplayReactor`, `ClientManager` (the whole core runtime, including
`formatTokenAmount`, plus the validation helpers) from `@ic-reactor/react`. Its
`react-server` export condition resolves to an entry that loads no React.
Hooks, `defineReactor`, `defineDisplayReactor`, `createReactorProvider`,
`createActorHooks`, the query/mutation factories, `skipToken`, the auth classes
and the identity-attribute helpers are missing exports there (`next build`:
"Export X doesn't exist in target module"), so server code builds a reactor
inside the request and calls `reactor.fetchQuery()` / `reactor.callMethod()`.
Importing from `@ic-reactor/core` still works, and is required with an RSC
bundler that ignores the `react-server` condition. The generated canister entry
(hooks and `factories: true` objects) imports hooks, so a server component
must not import it.

## Generated File Boundaries

Avoid hand-editing:

- `dist/`
- `.dfx/`, `.icp/`, `.mops/`
- `target/`
- `.next/`, `.astro/`
- `*.tsbuildinfo`
- generated canister declarations
- generated hook files

When generated hooks or declarations are wrong, fix `packages/codegen/src/` and
verify the affected CLI/Vite consumer.

## Verification

| Change type           | Commands                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docs only             | `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:ai-context`, `pnpm docs:build`, `pnpm docs:check-links`                    |
| AI context files      | `pnpm check:ai-context`                                                            |
| React hooks/factories | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/react test`                                             |
| Core runtime          | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/core test`                                              |
| React auth            | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/react test`                                             |
| Parser/candid         | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/parser build`, `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/candid test`  |
| Codegen               | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/codegen test` plus affected CLI/Vite checks             |
| Broad package change  | `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -b`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`                    |
| Package exports/build/module format | `pnpm verify:packages`                                               |
| Examples              | `pnpm typecheck:examples`, `pnpm build:examples`                                   |
| Docs site             | `pnpm docs:build`, `pnpm docs:check-links`                                                                  |

Do not run package build and package test concurrently when parser/candid tests
depend on parser `dist`; parser builds remove and recreate `dist`.

Script notes:

- `pnpm format:check` covers the whole repo; exclusions are declared in one
  place, `.prettierignore`, which the pre-commit hook honours too.
- `pnpm check:ai-context` is a CI gate. It asserts that the `llms.txt` version
  table matches each `package.json`, that every package but the parser ships a
  `packages/<name>/llms.txt`, and that no file listed in
  `scripts/ai-context-files.js` names a version no package is at or a docs path
  other than `/v3/`.
- `pnpm lint` is a CI gate. Run `pnpm build` first: the type-aware rules read
  core's emitted `.d.ts` through the workspace symlinks, and without a build
  they degrade to `any` and stop reporting. A new package needs a
  `tsconfig.typecheck.json` and an entry in `TYPECHECK_PROJECTS`.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs each package's own `typecheck` script plus `e2e/`'s and covers tests
  as well as `src`. The root `tsconfig.json` is references-only, so
  `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` at the root type-checks nothing.
- `pnpm verify:packages` packs every publishable package, installs the tarballs
  outside the workspace, imports/requires each entry point in real Node, and
  runs `publint` + `attw`. It is the only check that sees what consumers get.
- `pnpm build:examples` is a CI gate alongside `pnpm typecheck:examples`. `tsc`
  never loads a bundler, so a broken Vite/Next config type-checks clean; both
  Next.js examples were unbuildable while the type-check job stayed green.
